extension_metadata.note: Stress-test #7 finding: NYU publishes a full, itemized Cost of Attendance rather than a single tuition figure. Direct/billed items (tuition, health insurance, books, food, housing -- the latter two billed because on-campus housing is guaranteed for all 4 years) are captured as mandatory_fees_breakdown; non-billed planning estimates (transportation, personal expenses) are captured as estimated_living_costs_annual. Total of tuition_annual + mandatory_fees_annual + estimated_living_costs_annual = 68576 + 15838 + 5914 = 90328, matching NYU's own published 'Total Estimated Cost of Attendance: $90,328' exactly -- no EvidaPath-derived total was needed beyond the schema's own canonical fields, unlike TUM which required a second CostProfile record. Stress-test #10 finding: this single CostProfile record serves ALL applicants uniformly -- no UAE-national/non-UAE-national or domestic/international sticker-cost tier was found published. No blocked-account or visa proof-of-funds deposit requirement was found for UAE student visas in this run's research (see missing-data.json) -- this is a genuine structural difference from TUM's German blocked-account requirement, not yet independently confirmed absent by a UAE government immigration source, so it is NOT recorded as a VERIFIED ABSENCE here, only as an unresearched gap.

excerpt: Applicants use the Common Application, select New York University, and then have the option to be considered at one of our three degree-granting campuses: Abu Dhabi, New York City, or Shanghai (with the option to list up to two alternates). References apply through the 2027-2028 application cycle.

excerpt: NYU will remain test-optional through the 2027-2028 application cycle. Applicants are not required to submit standardized test scores. Results from standardized testing exams are an important criteria for evaluating our global pool of applicants. NYU maintains one of the most flexible testing policies of any college or university. Non-native English speakers must generally submit proficiency exam results from within two years prior, unless they have studied in English-only curricula for three consecutive years before applying. In general, most students for whom English is not their first language can expect to submit English language testing, even if they have been in a fully English-speaking curriculum. No specific curriculum requirements are listed; applicants come from a wide range of educational systems and backgrounds. Applicants must be 17 years old by August 1 of the year they plan to enroll.
